commit_message:
[CI] Build and validate the iree-base-core wheel in releases

The release pipeline builds, validates and uploads the compiler and
runtime wheels. Add iree-base-core, so that it is released with them
under the shared version:

* The candidate workflows compute its version like the other two and
  pass it on. `compute_common_version.py` takes the highest of the three
  `version.json` files, and now compares them as versions instead of as
  strings.
* `build_package.yml` builds the wheel in one Linux x86_64 job. It is
  pure Python, so the one wheel serves every platform and Python
  version. The existing steps attest it and upload it to the release.
* `validate_and_publish_release.yml` installs it and runs the new
  `iree.core._package_test`, as it does for the other two packages. The
  test imports every module of the installed package, which fails when
  the wheel misses a module or does not declare a dependency. The pkgci
  unit test job runs it too, because the release workflows do not run on
  pull requests.
* `pypi_deploy.sh` expects the wheel in a release.
* The release documentation lists the package.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Python] Run the Python tests with pytest

The Python tests were run as scripts that end in `unittest.main()`. A
test could therefore only be a `unittest` class, and what a test runner
offers (fixtures, selecting tests, reports, coverage) was not available.

Make pytest the runner. It runs `unittest` classes as they are, so no
test is rewritten:

* CMake: `iree_py_test` and `iree_local_py_test` run
  `python -m pytest <file>`, and `ARGS` are passed to pytest. With the
  new `SCRIPT` option a file is run as a script, as before. That option
  marks the files that pytest cannot run: the samples, the files that
  run their checks, disable themselves or exit when they are imported,
  and the tests that are configured through their own command line.
  The two tests of the profile tooling also stay scripts in CMake,
  because a build of the runtime alone installs no Python packages.
* Bazel: the new `iree_py_test` macro runs pytest through a small entry
  point. The tests of `iree.core`, of the profile renderer and of two
  build scripts use it. pytest is added to the Bazel pip lock.
* pkgci runs the tests of `iree.core` and the ONNX import test with
  pytest.
* pytest is added to the build requirements of the Python bindings.
  CMake warns once at configuration time when it is missing. The tests
  are still added and then fail, instead of going missing.
* `pytest.ini` marks the root of the tests, so that pytest does not pick
  up the configuration of a project that contains IREE.

Several tests set the log level to DEBUG in their `__main__` block,
which pytest does not run. CMake therefore passes `--log-level=DEBUG`,
so that a failed test still reports what it logged.

Four tests depended on being run as a script and now work under any
runner:

* `basic_test` and `net_test` of `iree.build` relied on being the
  `__main__` module, where `iree_build_main` looks up the entry points
  by default. They now pass their own module.
* `import_onnx_test` and `mnist_builder_test` skipped themselves in
  their `__main__` block when onnx is not installed. They now skip
  their test classes.

Of the 50 tests registered in CMake, 27 now run under pytest and 23 stay
scripts. The testing guide gets a section on Python tests.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

  pytest.

  are still added and then fail, instead of going missing.

  their `__main__` block when onnx is not installed. They now skip
  their test classes.

commit_message:
[Python] Add plugin loading helpers to iree.core

Add `iree.core.plugins`, the small part of plugin handling that the
compiler and runtime layers share. It is built on pluggy:

* `hookspec` and `hookimpl` are the markers for the hooks of a host and
  for their implementations in plugins. A plugin gets its marker from
  here and does not have to import the host.
* `create_plugin_manager` creates the manager for a host's hooks and
  loads the plugins that installed packages declare in an entry point
  group. Unlike pluggy's own loading, a plugin that fails to import or a
  distribution with unreadable metadata is skipped with a warning and
  does not keep the other plugins from loading.
* `merge_plugin_mappings` merges the name-to-value mappings that the
  plugins return from a hook, and rejects a name that more than one
  plugin provides.

A host loads every plugin to learn what it provides, so a plugin module
must be cheap to import. The module documents the rule that follows:
a plugin provides factories, and only calling a factory imports a heavy
dependency such as an ML framework. A test covers that pattern.

pluggy becomes a dependency of the iree-base-core wheel: a version range
in `pyproject.toml`, and an exact version with hashes in the generated
lock files.

Nothing uses these helpers yet: the compiler and runtime layers will
declare their hooks with them.

commit_message:
[Python] Add log sink setup for applications to iree.core

Add `iree.core.log_config.configure_application_logging`, for the entry
point of an application built on these packages: it sends Loguru
messages to stderr or to a rotating file, with a level and a format.

Libraries only emit messages, and where those go is up to the
application. As Loguru intends for an application, the helper replaces
all sinks, including the stderr sink that Loguru installs by itself, so
a second call replaces the sink of the first. An application that sets
up Loguru itself does not call it.

File sinks are written without color codes, braces in a file name are
kept, and a process without a stderr is handled. Whether to color stderr
is left to Loguru.

Loguru becomes a dependency of the iree-base-core wheel: a version range
in `pyproject.toml`, and an exact version with hashes, together with
what it needs on Windows, in the generated lock files.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[Python] Add log sink setup for applications to iree.core

Add `iree.core.log_config.configure_application_logging`, for the entry
point of an application built on these packages: it sends Loguru
messages to stderr or to a rotating file, with a level and a format.

Libraries only emit messages, and where those go is up to the
application. As Loguru intends for an application, the helper replaces
all sinks, including the stderr sink that Loguru installs by itself, so
a second call replaces the sink of the first. An application that sets
up Loguru itself does not call it.

File sinks are written without color codes, braces in a file name are
kept, and a process without a stderr is handled. Whether to color stderr
is left to Loguru.

Loguru becomes a dependency of the iree-base-core wheel: a version range
in `pyproject.toml`, and an exact version with hashes, together with
what it needs on Windows, in the generated lock files.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Python] Add log sink setup for applications to iree.core

Add `iree.core.log_config.configure_application_logging`, for the entry
point of an application built on these packages: it sends Loguru
messages to stderr or to a rotating file, with a level and a format.

Libraries only emit messages, and where those go is up to the
application. As Loguru intends for an application, the helper replaces
all sinks, including the stderr sink that Loguru installs by itself, so
a second call replaces the sink of the first. An application that sets
up Loguru itself does not call it.

File sinks are written without color codes, braces in a file name are
kept, and a process without a stderr is handled. Whether to color stderr
is left to Loguru.

in `pyproject.toml`, and an exact version with hashes, together with
what it needs on Windows, in the generated lock files.

commit_message:
[Python] Add log sink setup for applications to iree.core

Add `iree.core.log_config.configure_application_logging`, for the entry
point of an application built on these packages: it sends Loguru
messages to stderr or to a rotating file, with a level and a format.

Libraries only emit messages, and where those go is up to the
application. As Loguru intends for an application, the helper replaces
all sinks, including the stderr sink that Loguru installs by itself, so
a second call replaces the sink of the first. An application that sets
up Loguru itself does not call it.

File sinks are written without color codes, braces in a file name are
kept, and a process without a stderr is handled. Whether to color stderr
is left to Loguru.

Loguru becomes a dependency of the iree-base-core wheel: a version range
in `pyproject.toml`, and an exact version with hashes, together with
what it needs on Windows, in the generated lock files.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: Test Android / android_arm64

commit_message:
[Runtime] Add NEON conv_nchwc ukernel tile for arm_64 (#25290)

Adds an baseline arm_64 NEON tile kernel for the data-tiled convolution
microkernel, with inner tile sizes (OW_TILE=8, K0=8, C0=8). This is the
(OC, IC) = (8, 8) inner tile the compiler already selects for f32
convolutions on AArch64, which until now fell back to the generic tile
function.

Layouts (c0 = inner IC block, k0 = inner OC block):
    input [N, IC/c0, H, W, c0]
    filter [OC/k0, IC/c0, FH, FW, c0, k0]
    output [N, OC/k0, OH, OW, k0]

The kernel uses 16 NEON accumulators and processes input channels in
groups of 4, using vfmaq_laneq_f32 for efficient FMLA execution. A new
IREE_UK_UNROLL_DISABLE macro prevents unrolling the inner loop to avoid
register spills.

The kernel uses only NEON instructions available on every aarch64 cpu.
The ABI and generic fallback remain unchanged.

Only f32 is supported for now; other types and tile shapes are left for
future work.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Pooja Hemashekar <hemashekar@roofline.ai>
name: setup_metadata
